## What CodeSquad Does

CodeSquad builds connected growth systems for clinics, med spas and e-commerce brands — ads, instant follow-up, CRM dashboards, SEO/AEO/GEO and marketing intelligence, built into the client's existing stack. The pitch is explicitly "no rip-and-replace, no new tools to learn": CodeSquad connects to the booking system, store platform or CRM a client already uses rather than forcing a migration.

Core capabilities (from the homepage "What We Do" section):
- **Websites & software** — fast, modern sites, web apps and custom platforms built to convert and scale.
- **CRM & dashboards** — every lead, deal and campaign tracked in one live view.
- **Ads — Google & Meta** — intent-driven campaigns and landing pages.
- **SEO · AEO · GEO** — get found on Google and recommended by AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Gemini.
- **AI agents & automation** — instant follow-up, nurture and internal workflows that run without the client's team.
- **Marketing intelligence** — spend, ROAS, LTV and content performance unified across every connected platform.

By-the-numbers (from live client dashboards, cited on the homepage):
- 20+ companies served
- 3-second average lead response time
- 15+ platforms unified (ENERGYbits marketing-intelligence build)
- 100% message delivery logged

Clients/brands referenced publicly: iPromo, ENERGYbits, Gengyve USA, Modern Law, Kenetics Solutions, TriState Auto Sales, SettleIn, Mama's Compass, Debate Partners, Harmony Med Spa, CareInn Dental Clinic, RTM Kinetics, Law Signal.

## How the Process Works (Build then Grow)

CodeSquad's engagement model is two phases: a one-time **Build**, then a monthly **Grow** retainer. The same model applies across every industry, configured for it.

**Phase 1 · Build (one-time):** audit what the client has, design the system, launch it, train the team. Includes: discovery call, audit & opportunity assessment, growth strategy, CRM & stack setup, website & landing pages, automations & follow-up flows, campaign launch, team training.

**Phase 2 · Grow (monthly retainer):** run the system, optimize it every month, report exactly what it's producing. Includes: ad management, ongoing optimization, content & SEO·AEO·GEO, nurture & retention campaigns, reporting dashboard, ongoing support.

**Pricing model:** a one-time build fee, then a monthly growth retainer with no long-term lock-in. Third-party tools and subscriptions (hosting, ad spend, CRM licences, SMS/email credits, APIs) are billed separately — not included in the package. No setup fee beyond the build; month-to-month; cancel anytime.

**The 5-step delivery timeline** (same steps shown on the homepage and /process):
1. **Discovery Call** — learn the business, workflows, goals and bottlenecks: where growth is leaking and why.
2. **Opportunity Assessment** — map the highest-impact automation and AI opportunities, ranked by business value and ROI.
3. **Build & Deploy** — implement the systems, AI agents and workflows directly into the stack already in use.
4. **Launch & Train** — everything goes live, documented and connected, with the team trained to run it confidently.
5. **Optimize & Scale** — keep improving and expanding the system as the business grows, as an ongoing AI partner.

**Process-page FAQ:**
- *How long does the build take?* Depends on scope (campaigns, pages, integrations needed). A timeline is given after the opportunity assessment, before any build work starts; campaigns only launch once tracking and follow-up are tested end to end.
- *Is there a long-term contract?* No. The build is a one-time fee; after launch, clients move to a monthly growth retainer with no long-term lock-in.
- *What's included, and what isn't?* Build covers audit, strategy, CRM/stack setup, website/landing pages, automations, campaign launch, team training. Retainer covers ad management, optimization, content & SEO/AEO/GEO, nurture/retention campaigns, reporting, support. Third-party tools (ad spend, CRM licences, SMS/email credits) are billed separately.
- *Do I have to switch the software I already use?* No. CodeSquad builds into the existing stack — booking system, store platform or CRM — connecting what already works rather than migrating it.

Most clients keep CodeSquad on after launch as their ongoing AI partner, with monthly strategy sessions and evolving systems.

## Industry Solutions

One connected growth engine, configured for three fields: Aesthetics/Medical Clinics, E-commerce, and IT & Engineering. The shared wins across all three: reach the right buyer, respond before anyone else, and never lose a lead already paid for — via campaigns built per offer, instant automated follow-up, and content that ranks and converts (SEO/AEO/GEO published from the same dashboard as leads and sales).

Proof strip (from a live clinic dashboard, most recent 90-day window): 3s speed to lead · 4.25% click-through rate · $60 cost per lead · 100% email delivery.

### Aesthetics / Medical Clinics (med spas, aesthetic clinics, laser clinics, cosmetic derm)

Headline: "Every enquiry answered in 60 seconds. More booked patients." Treatment-based Google Ads, instant follow-up and booking in one system, built into the booking software already in use (e.g. PatientNow — no migration).

Real client numbers cited (live client, 2-month window): 60+ leads generated · ~$50 cost per lead · 6–7 new patients booked · 3s lead response time · 14-day automated nurture.

Sample campaign types built for this audience: Local ("Med Spa Near Me – [City]", "Aesthetic Clinic – [Neighborhood]", "Med Spa Open Weekends"), Treatment (Medical Weight Loss/GLP-1, Botox & Fillers, Laser Hair Removal, Facials & Microneedling, IV Vitamin Therapy, Skin Tightening & Body Contouring), and Ranking plays (owning "Best Botox [City]", "Best Lip Filler [City]", "Best Med Spa [City]" via landing page + blog).

Why-us pitch: "Tired of agencies that don't understand your practice?" — booked patients (not clicks) traced to the exact ad/keyword, no software switching required, three years with healthcare brands with health-ad compliance built in by default.

FAQ highlights: No need to switch booking system (Harmony kept PatientNow). Response within seconds day or night by SMS/email, with a 14-day nurture that stops the instant a patient books. Pricing is a one-time build fee + monthly growth retainer, no long-term lock-in; third-party tools billed separately. Campaigns follow Google's restricted-health-advertising rules; conversions only count confirmed leads.

### Clinics & Dental Practices (small medical clinics, dental practices)

Headline: "Every patient enquiry answered in 60 seconds. A fuller appointment book." Local Google Ads, instant follow-up and online booking built into the practice software already in use. Same real-client numbers as Aesthetics (60+ leads/2 months, ~$50 CPL, 6–7 new patients, 3s response, 14-day nurture) — drawn from the same Harmony Med Spa system example, shown here for the clinics/dental audience.

Sample campaigns — Medical clinic track: Clinic Near Me, Walk-In Clinic, Doctor Accepting New Patients, Weight Loss Program (GLP-1), IV Therapy & Wellness, Physio & Back Pain, Health Check-Ups, Hormone Replacement Therapy, Pediatric & Family Care, plus "Best Clinic/Weight Loss Clinic/Walk-In Clinic [City]" ranking plays.
Sample campaigns — Dental track: Dentist Near Me, Weekend Dentist, Dental Implants, Invisalign & Aligners, Teeth Whitening & Veneers, Emergency Dental, Root Canal Therapy, Pediatric Dentistry, plus "Best Dentist/Implant Dentist/Invisalign [City]" ranking plays.

Why-us pitch: "Tired of agencies that have never run a clinic?" — booked appointments traced to ad/keyword/campaign, keep existing practice-management/scheduling software, campaigns for check-ups/implants/aligners/urgent visits run within health-advertising rules from day one.

Proof quotes: Harmony Med Spa ("CodeSquad connected our ads, CRM and follow-up into one system... nothing slips through"), CareInn Dental Clinic ("We went live with the whole system already running... the schedule filled from day one").

FAQ highlights mirror the Aesthetics page: no software switch required, seconds-fast response with 14-day nurture, one-time build fee + monthly retainer pricing with no lock-in, health-advertising-rule compliant.

### E-commerce

Headline: "Turn traffic into revenue. Buyers into regulars." For online stores and DTC brands — Shopping ads, cart recovery and post-purchase flows in one system.

Problem framing: roughly 7 in 10 carts are abandoned and most buyers never return; the revenue is already in the funnel, it just isn't being recovered. Three leak points addressed: abandoned carts (automated cart/browse-abandon flows bring shoppers back via SMS/email within minutes), one-time buyers (post-purchase and win-back sequences turn a single sale into a habit), and blind ad spend (every campaign tied to real orders and LTV, not platform-reported ROAS).

Package includes: conversion-optimized store design & support, product & category SEO, local SEO, Google Shopping & search ads management, social media content & management, AI automation for carts & follow-up, email & SMS marketing flows, unified analytics/ROAS/LTV reporting, ongoing technical support. Pricing: no setup fee, month-to-month, cancel anytime; ad spend/platform apps/email credits billed separately.

### IT & Engineering

Headline: "Engineering-grade software, systems & automation." For IT & engineering teams — web, CRM, AI, automation and IoT, plus SEO/AEO/GEO, built into the existing stack and owned by the client's team. Plans from $499/mo.

Package includes: custom website design/build/deployment, CRM setup with pipeline & lead capture, automation for leads & onboarding, AI agents & custom workflow automation, SEO/AEO/GEO for Google and AI search, monthly performance reporting. Third-party tools/subscriptions billed separately. No setup fee, month-to-month, cancel anytime.

Problem framing: technical companies build great things, then lose hours to manual work, cold inbound leads, and disconnected tools. Three levers addressed: manual/repetitive work (AI agents and automations remove onboarding/reporting/data-entry busywork), slow inbound response (instant follow-up wired into a real CRM), invisible in AI & search (SEO/AEO/GEO make the product quotable to both Google and AI assistants).

What's built: (1) **Web & software development** — Next.js/React front-ends on typed back-ends, marketing sites, customer portals, custom web apps, secure API integrations. (2) **CRM & business systems** — pipeline/deal stages, automatic lead routing, quoting/onboarding/support workflows, live revenue/pipeline dashboards. (3) **AI agents & automation** — AI assistants for support/sales/research, workflow automation, document/data/reporting pipelines. (4) **IoT & connected systems** — device/sensor data collection, real-time monitoring dashboards & alerting, CRM/ops integration. (5) **SEO · AEO · GEO** — technical SEO, site speed, structured data, AEO content AI Overviews can quote, GEO so ChatGPT & Gemini surface the product. (6) **Lead generation & ads** — Google & LinkedIn campaigns for B2B intent, demo/RFP-tuned landing pages, speed-to-lead follow-up.

## Case Studies (Full Text)

### Harmony MedSpa — Patient Growth Automation for Medical Spas
**Industry:** Medical Aesthetics · **Services:** Automation, SEO · **URL:** /case-studies/harmony-medspa-patient-growth-automation

Stats: 20+ hours/week saved on manual follow-up · 24/7 automated lead capture and follow-up · 5-touch structured follow-up for non-booking leads · 1 live dashboard.

**Challenge:** Harmony MedSpa delivered excellent patient care, but lead management depended heavily on manual follow-up. Enquiries arrived around the clock via website forms, phone, Google Ads and other channels; because the inbox was checked manually between appointments, potential patients could wait hours for a response. There was no structured follow-up for people who enquired but didn't book — once a lead went cold it was often never contacted again. Past patients weren't systematically re-engaged, rebooking reminders were inconsistent, and referrals weren't tracked end to end. Management had no single view of leads, communications, follow-up status or marketing performance. The clinical experience was strong; the operational challenge was speed, consistency and visibility.

**Solution:** CodeSquad built a connected system that captures every lead, responds within 60 seconds, follows up automatically over 14 days, reactivates past patients, and manages rebooking and referrals — all visible on one live dashboard used daily. Stack: Website + Make.com + Airtable + Mandrill + Mailchimp + PatientNow + custom dashboard.

**Key capabilities:** Capture (every lead across channels) · Respond & Nurture (automated across 14 days) · Track (full visibility in one dashboard).

**Modeled revenue estimate** (illustrative, based on published industry benchmarks, not Harmony's reported figures): manual follow-up typically books 8–12% of enquiries; automated 60-second response with structured follow-up books 25–35%. Average med spa visit runs $420–500. For a clinic receiving 80 enquiries/month: before ≈ 8 booked appointments, after ≈ 22 booked appointments, difference ≈ 14 appointments/month ≈ $5,900–7,000 in additional first-visit revenue.

**Before → After:** Response time: hours → under 60 seconds. Follow-up: 20+ hrs/week → under 2. Non-booker follow-up: none → 5-touch automated sequence. Past-patient re-engagement: none → automated by treatment cycle. Visibility: multiple tools → 1 live dashboard.

**Quote:** "CodeSquad has done great work transitioning us from fragmented follow-up to a fully automated system." — Hayden, Harmony MedSpa

**Conclusion:** The missing piece was never treatment quality — it was a reliable system for responding, following up, re-engaging and tracking every patient opportunity, built without replacing the clinic's existing booking process.

### CareInn Dental Clinic — Patient Growth Automation for Dental Clinics
**Industry:** Dental Care · **Services:** Automation, SEO, Patient Growth · **URL:** /case-studies/careinn-dental-clinic

Stats: system live before the first patient (from day one) · 24/7 automated lead capture and follow-up · 5 touches of structured follow-up over 14 days · 1 live dashboard from day one.

**Challenge:** CareInn launched with no existing patient pipeline, no history of leads, no established follow-up habits and no base of returning patients. Every new patient had to come from website enquiries, phone calls or referrals — with real risk of losing early momentum before the clinic built a reputation, since there was no existing base to fall back on.

**Solution:** CodeSquad built CareInn's patient-growth system from the ground up, live before day one of operation. It captures every lead, responds within 60 seconds, follows up automatically over 14 days, and gives the team full visibility. Stack: Website + Make.com + Airtable + SMS + Email + custom dashboard.

**Key capabilities:** Launch-ready (live before the first patient) · Respond & Nurture (every enquiry answered and followed up automatically) · Grow (patient volume tracked and growing from day one).

**Before → After:** Patient pipeline: none at launch → live from day one. Response time: no process → under 60 seconds. Follow-up: none → 14-day automated sequence. Visibility: none → 1 live dashboard. Patient volume: starting from zero → growing steadily since launch.

**Conclusion:** CareInn never had a gap to fix — every enquiry since launch has gone through the same connected pipeline (captured, answered, followed up, tracked in one place), which is why patient volume has grown since day one.

**FAQ:** Will this replace our booking system? No — it wraps around the existing system. What if we already have a marketing team? The Dashboard tier fits teams that just need visibility. How long to launch? 2–3 weeks.

### ENERGYbits — Marketing Intelligence Across a Complex DTC Stack
**Industry:** DTC Wellness · **Services:** Marketing Intelligence · **URL:** /case-studies/energybits

Stats: 15+ platforms connected · 3 search scores (SEO/AEO/GEO) · 1 intelligence layer · pre-publish content validation.

**Challenge:** Performance and content data was spread across 15+ platforms. Marketing context was distributed across ad, analytics and content tools; research/drafting/quality checks required repeated manual effort; content needed to perform in both traditional search and AI-generated answers.

**Solution:** A connected marketing-intelligence platform with automated blog pipelines and SEO/AEO/GEO scoring before content goes live. (1) Connected intelligence — signals from 15+ platforms feed a shared decision layer. (2) Automated blog pipeline — research and structured drafting move through a consistent production flow. (3) Pre-publish scoring — every draft evaluated for search, answer-engine and generative-engine readiness.

**Key capabilities:** Data connection (15+ platform integrations, normalised signals, unified analysis) · Content automation (research pipeline, structured drafting, editorial workflow) · Discoverability (SEO/AEO/GEO scoring).

**Results:** Quality checks happen earlier (content evaluated before publication). A scalable content operation (output increases without multiplying manual research/coordination). Visibility beyond traditional search (workflow accounts for both search engines and AI answer experiences).

### iPromo — Automated Product Marketing for B2B E-commerce
**Industry:** B2B E-commerce · **Services:** Image Automation, Salesforce · **URL:** /case-studies/ipromo

Stats: 25+ years in business (client) · 1 connected pipeline · automated product imagery · faster campaign launch.

**Challenge:** Product-of-the-month campaigns required repetitive image work, data enrichment, analysis and coordination between sales and marketing systems — manual image production, disconnected customer data between campaign inputs and Salesforce, and limited analysis before teams could act.

**Solution:** An automated image and campaign pipeline enriching product data, preparing creative assets, and connecting the result to Salesforce and email workflows. (1) Automated creative production — campaign-ready product imagery generated through a consistent workflow. (2) Salesforce integration — customer/product context moves into the campaign without duplicate entry. (3) Built-in enrichment — product information prepared and analysed before launch.

**Key capabilities:** Creative automation (product image pipeline, campaign formatting, asset quality checks) · CRM workflow (Salesforce connection, record enrichment, campaign handoff) · Marketing operations (email-ready outputs, repeatable monthly process, performance analysis).

**Results:** Faster path to market (monthly campaigns from selection to launch with fewer manual steps). Consistent campaign assets (every product follows the same creative workflow). Sales and marketing connected (campaign execution uses customer/product context already in Salesforce).

**Quote:** "Shahzaib did a great job of communicating throughout the project. He found solutions to hurdles along the way and ultimately we were very satisfied with the results." — Jon, iPromo

### GengyveUSA — One Intelligence Layer for a Healthcare Commerce Brand
**Industry:** Healthcare E-commerce · **Services:** SEO, Ads, Content · **URL:** /case-studies/gengyveusa

Stats: 3 growth channels unified · 1 automation layer · always-on review analysis · clearer marketing decisions.

**Challenge:** SEO, advertising, content and customer reviews produced valuable signals, but they were isolated across tools: channel silos between organic and paid teams, unstructured review feedback hard to analyse at scale, and slow decisions from reporting overhead.

**Solution:** A unified automation layer connecting search, ads, content and customer sentiment for this veteran-owned oral-care brand. (1) Unified marketing view — cross-channel signals organised around the decisions the team needs. (2) Automated review intelligence — customer feedback grouped into recurring themes and opportunities. (3) Actionable content inputs — search/ad insights inform next content priorities.

**Key capabilities:** Search intelligence (SEO monitoring, content opportunity discovery) · Performance signals (paid-media campaign data, cross-channel context, decision support) · Customer voice (review analysis, theme detection, messaging insights).

**Results:** One source of marketing context (content, ads, search and feedback visibly influence each other). Less reporting overhead (automated analysis replaces repetitive data assembly). Sharper priorities (growth decisions grounded in connected signals).

### Modern Law — A Content Engine Built for a Multi-Brand Law Firm
**Industry:** Family Law · **Services:** Content Automation · **URL:** /case-studies/modern-law

Stats: 4 brands connected · 1 unified workflow · always-on content production · less manual coordination.

**Challenge:** Four distinct legal brands needed a consistent stream of content, but every article/image/social post meant another handoff for an already busy team — scattered production across disconnected tools, brand consistency pressure without multiplying workload, and slow repurposing of good ideas into full campaigns.

**Solution:** A central automation system turning approved ideas into coordinated blog, social and visual content for every brand. (1) One content pipeline — structured workflow from brief to review and publication. (2) Multi-brand intelligence — rules preserve each brand's audience, tone and legal context. (3) Automated repurposing — long-form content becomes platform-ready social posts and image prompts automatically.

**Key capabilities:** Content operations (central publishing queue, approval checkpoints, reusable campaign briefs) · AI automation (draft generation, social repurposing, visual asset prompts) · Governance (brand-specific guardrails, human review, status visibility).

**Results:** A repeatable publishing system (production run as an operation, not rebuilt per campaign). More output from every idea (one topic feeds multiple brands/formats/channels). Control stays with the team (automation handles production, SMEs keep final approval).

**Quote:** "Working with Shahzaib was the ideal experience. He was knowledgeable, solutions oriented, and incredibly communicative... We'll definitely be working with him again." — Sarah, Modern Law

### TriState Auto Sales — Omnichannel Customer Engagement Platform
**Industry:** Automotive Retail · **Services:** Chatbot Automation, CRM Integration, Lead Routing · **URL:** /case-studies/tristate-auto-sales

Stats: omnichannel (website chat, social media and phone in one flow) · 1 CRM for every conversation/ticket/lead · automated routing, follow-up and appointment booking.

**Challenge:** TriState fielded customer questions across website chat, social media and phone with no single system tying them together. Every conversation started from scratch; staff manually triaged requests and qualified leads with no shared source of truth linking conversations to the CRM, so leads could sit unrouted. Appointment booking and follow-up were handled by hand.

**Solution:** A connected omnichannel engagement system built around TriState's existing operation. An AI chatbot handles first-touch conversations across every channel, using natural-language query classification to understand whether a message is a question, support ticket or sales inquiry, and routes it accordingly. Every conversation/ticket/lead flows into one CRM, kept in sync automatically, with follow-up and appointment booking handled by the same system.

**Key capabilities:** Engage (omnichannel chatbot answers/routes every conversation) · Qualify (leads scored and routed into the CRM) · Follow up (appointments booked, follow-ups sent automatically).

**Quote:** "Outstanding work on the TriState omnichannel platform. The integration was seamless and the system performs reliably. Great communication throughout the project." — TriState Team

### RTM Kinetics — Patient Management & Remote Monitoring for Physical Therapy
**Industry:** Remote Patient Monitoring · **Services:** Patient CRM, Remote Monitoring, Automation · **URL:** /case-studies/rtm-kinetics

Stats: 1 CRM for the full patient lifecycle · automated reconnect campaigns for quiet leads · real-time recovery and feedback tracking.

**Challenge:** RTM Kinetics needed to manage the full patient relationship — from first enquiry through active rehabilitation — but it lived across disconnected tools. Leads, contact history and reconnect campaigns for patients who'd gone quiet were tracked separately from the exercise/recovery data therapists needed. Patient feedback was collected inconsistently, making it hard to spot problems early or show program impact.

**Solution:** A connected system spanning the full patient lifecycle. It manages the patient CRM end to end — capturing leads, automating reconnect campaigns for quiet patients, and collecting structured feedback — while syncing with the platform's remote-monitoring tools so therapists have one place to see the full picture. Stack: React/Node.js + PostgreSQL + SMS/Email automation + remote monitoring integration.

**Key capabilities:** Capture (every lead tracked through one CRM pipeline) · Reconnect (automated re-engagement for quiet patients) · Monitor (feedback and recovery data in one dashboard).

**Quote:** "I had the pleasure of working with Shahzaib on developing an AI platform, where he showcased exceptional technical skills, creativity, and professionalism... highly collaborative, communicative, and consistently delivered high-quality work on time." — Kennard Smith, RTM

### Law Signal — Media & Case Management Automation for Law Firms
**Industry:** Legal Media Automation · **Services:** Video Automation, PR, CRM Sync · **URL:** /case-studies/law-signal

Stats: case files turned into video and press content automatically · CRM and back office synced with media output · SEO and AEO publishing built into every release.

SEO/AEO publishing was handled separately from media work, and the back office/CRM weren't synced with media output.

**Solution:** An automated pipeline connecting case files directly to publish-ready media. The back office and CRM stay synced throughout. Stack: Node.js automation pipeline + video generation + CRM sync + SEO/AEO publishing layer.

**Key capabilities:** Auto-Produce (case files → press-ready videos automatically) · Distribute (press releases/media synced across channels) · Publish (SEO/AEO-optimized publishing built in).

**Quote:** "I worked with Shah on a number of projects and was consistently impressed by his ability to break down complex problems into tractable pieces and drive them to completion... reliable under pressure, which matters more than anything once things get real." — Lou, Law Signal

**Industry:** Comparison & Aggregation · **Services:** Product Aggregation, AI Scoring, SEO Content · **URL:** /case-studies/mamas-compass

Pulling details/pricing/stock by hand didn't scale, and manually written comparisons couldn't keep pace with price/product changes. Customer feedback was scattered and didn't feed back into scoring.

Customer feedback feeds back into scoring; affiliate links are managed automatically. Stack: Node.js data pipeline + AI scoring/ML + SEO content generation + affiliate link management.

**Key capabilities:** Aggregate (product data pulled from multiple sources automatically) · Compare (AI scoring ranks/compares products) · Optimize (SEO content generated to match search intent).

### SettleIn — Eligibility & Document Processing Platform
**Industry:** Document & Eligibility Processing · **Services:** OCR, Document Processing, Eligibility Scoring · **URL:** /case-studies/settlein

Stats: documents read and processed via OCR automatically · eligibility determined automatically against criteria · every application tracked in one dashboard.

**Challenge:** SettleIn needed to process a high volume of applicant documents, but manual reading/evaluation didn't scale. Documents arrived in inconsistent formats requiring manual review before any eligibility assessment could start; scoring was subjective and slow when manual, and applicants waited without visibility into case status.

**Solution:** An automated document-to-decision pipeline. OCR extracts information directly from uploaded documents, eligibility scoring runs automatically against the relevant criteria, and AI-assisted feedback tells applicants where they stand. An admin dashboard gives the team oversight of every application, with tracking that keeps each case moving without manual chasing. Stack: OCR/document understanding + AI eligibility scoring + admin dashboard + application tracking.

**Key capabilities:** Extract (OCR pulls information from uploaded documents) · Score (eligibility determined automatically against criteria) · Track (every application visible in one dashboard).

**Quote:** "I highly recommend Shahzaib and Code Squad. They were diligent, prompt and reliable..." — Faraz Siddiqui O., SettleIn

### Debate Partners — Competitive Debate Platform & Case Management
**Industry:** Competitive Debate Platform · **Services:** AI Case Generation, CRM, Billing · **URL:** /case-studies/debate-partners

Stats: sources analyzed and turned into cases automatically · multi-format support (Policy, LD, Public Forum) · teams, cases and billing connected in one platform.

**Challenge:** Debate Partners needed to turn raw research into competition-ready cases, but the process was almost entirely manual — cross-referencing sources by hand, compiling evidence packets, tracking citations separately, none of it scaling across formats (Policy, LD, Public Forum). Team/coach management sat in a different system from case-building, and subscriptions/billing were separate again.

**Solution:** A connected case-generation and team-management platform. It analyzes and cross-references source documents automatically, generates debate cases with evidence packets and citations attached, and supports multiple competitive formats out of the box. A CRM keeps teams and coaches organized, with subscription management and billing on the same platform. Stack: document analysis/cross-referencing + AI case generation + CRM + subscription billing.

**Key capabilities:** Analyze (sources cross-referenced automatically for evidence) · Generate (debate cases built with citations attached) · Manage (CRM and billing for teams/coaches in one place).

**Quote:** "Excellent developing a complex AI-driven application from scratch, over an extended period of time." — Michael, Debate Partners

**Shared case-study FAQ (appears across several case studies):** Will this replace our existing platform? No — it wraps around the existing system. What if we already have a marketing team? The Dashboard tier fits teams that just need visibility. How long to launch? 2–3 weeks.

## Blog Articles (Full Text / Extended Summaries)

### Your SaaS Is Being Recommended by AI — But Is It Being Recommended to Your Customers?
*AEO / SEO · September 2, 2026 · /blog/saas-ai-recommendations-seo-ai-search*

For roughly two decades, SEO strategy was: rank, get the click, convert, win the customer. AI-powered discovery introduces a different question — can an AI system understand a company well enough to confidently recommend it? Buyers increasingly ask an AI assistant to narrow their options before ever reaching a search results page; ranking #1 on Google does not guarantee an AI recommendation.

SaaS is especially exposed because software buying naturally involves comparison, review-platform/aggregator authority already feeds AI answers, and SaaS buying cycles involve extensive multi-stakeholder research that AI compresses.

**The 7 strategies to get recommended by AI:**
1. **Write in extractable units** — put the answer near the start of each section; use descriptive H2s/H3s; use tables/lists for specs, pricing, limits, comparisons.
2. **Publish original data** — anonymized usage data, benchmarks, adoption trends or industry research that other companies can't reproduce.
3. **Own your comparison and alternatives pages** — objective tables explaining where each product wins/falls short, not pure sales copy.
4. **Make pricing information accessible** — exact pricing if possible, otherwise ranges, plan structures, seat minimums or per-user costs.
5. **Show your experts** — named authors, credentials, expert quotes, methodology notes, a real About page.
6. **Build a strong third-party presence** — accurate, consistent profiles on review platforms, directories, publications, communities and podcasts; genuine reviews.
7. **Define the category you want to be found in** — use the language customers actually use to describe the problem and where the product fits.

**90-day rollout:** Days 1–30 — ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI features the questions buyers ask; record which brands appear; audit top pages for clarity/structure/author info. Days 31–60 — fix comparison/pricing/author pages, start an original research project. Days 61–90 — publish and promote the research, refresh third-party profiles, re-test visibility.

**Metrics to track beyond traffic:** share of AI mentions, citation accuracy, branded search volume, AI referral traffic, signup quality, review velocity.

**5 mistakes:** mass-producing thin content, gating your best content behind forms, hiding pricing, ignoring inaccurate AI descriptions of your product, abandoning traditional SEO entirely.

**Bottom line:** Brands that win aren't the ones publishing the most — they're the ones that make information easy to understand, verify and reference. "Search did not disappear. It gained an interpreter."

### SEO Isn't Dead — But Your SaaS SEO Playbook Probably Is
*AI Automation / AEO-SEO · August 13, 2026 · /blog/ai-seo-for-saas*

Subtitle: "AI SEO for SaaS: How to Rank in Google and Get Recommended by ChatGPT, Claude, and AI Overviews."

**Key takeaways:** software discovery has moved upstream (many buyers ask AI assistants before traditional search); rankings and AI citations are different (a page can rank highly and still be absent from an AI recommendation); AI assistants favor content that's easy to understand/verify (clear structure, original data, named experts, transparent pricing, credible third-party sources); comparison/alternatives/pricing pages are high-value because they directly answer what buyers ask AI; measure more than traffic (AI mentions, citation accuracy, branded search growth, referral traffic, assisted signups).

Covers the same 7-tactic framework as the companion article above (extractable units, original data, comparison pages, accessible pricing, named experts, third-party presence, clear category definition) plus the same 90-day rollout plan and the same "5 mistakes that quietly hurt visibility." Distinguishes traditional SEO ("can a search engine find and rank this page?") from AI search optimization ("can an AI system understand this page, extract a claim, and confidently associate it with your company?").

**FAQ:** Is SEO dead for SaaS? No — it remains the foundation; AI discovery changes the search journey, not the need for strong SEO. How is AI search optimization different from regular SEO? More emphasis on structure, extractability, original evidence, verifiable claims. Can I pay to appear in AI answers? Organic recommendations differ from any sponsored placements some platforms may offer. How long before I see results? Structural fixes can help quickly; authority-building (reviews, research, coverage) takes longer. What if an AI tool describes my product incorrectly? Make correct information clear and consistent across your site and third-party profiles.

### I Used Claude to Turn a Messy Spreadsheet Into a Useful Dashboard
*AI Automation · August 12, 2026 · /blog/claude-messy-spreadsheet-to-dashboard*

A first-person account of handing a chaotic sales-tracking spreadsheet to Claude instead of manually untangling it over a weekend. The spreadsheet had dates in four different formats, inconsistent region names ("New York"/"NY"/"N.Y."), revenue stored as mixed text/numbers, duplicate rows from copy-pasted updates, and ambiguous empty cells.

**Step 1 — Diagnose:** Uploaded the sheet and asked "What's going on in this data, and what would need to happen before it's usable?" Claude returned a concrete list of inconsistent columns, likely duplicates, missing-value counts and duplicate-meaning columns before touching anything.

**Step 2 — Clean:** Standardized dates to one format, merged regional-name variants, converted revenue to real numbers, flagged duplicates for human confirmation before removing them, and clearly marked missing values instead of leaving blank cells. Every change was explained, which caught one or two places where an assumption (e.g. about "New York") needed correction.

**Step 3 — Insights:** Once clean, asked what patterns stood out — surfaced one underrated region quietly outperforming others, and a seasonal dip in a product line that had been misread internally as an ongoing decline.

**Iteration:** Swapping a bar chart for a trend line, grouping categories, or highlighting the top three reps instead of top ten each took a sentence, not a rebuild — "less like using a tool and more like working with someone who understood what I was trying to see."

**Lessons:** most "data problems" are consistency problems; explaining changes builds trust as much as making them; a dashboard is only useful if it's easy to adjust; you don't need to be a data analyst to get analyst-quality output — you just need to know what questions you want answered.

### One Prompt, One Studio: How HyperFrames + Claude Turn Anyone Into a Video Editor
*AI Automation · August 10, 2026 · /blog/hyperframes-claude-ai-video-creation-guide*

HyperFrames is a free, open-source video framework built by HeyGen. Paired with Claude Code (Anthropic's AI coding agent), it writes, animates and renders professional video from a plain-English prompt — no timeline, no editing software, no design background required. (Also compatible with Cursor, Gemini CLI and Codex.)

**Mac setup (~15 min, one-time):** install Node.js, install Homebrew, `brew install ffmpeg`, create a project folder (e.g. `~/Documents/AI-Videos`), open Claude Code inside it and run `npx hyperframes skills update` then restart Claude Code, then `npx hyperframes preview` for a live browser preview and export to MP4/MOV/WebM.

**Example:** a single prompt describing a dark background, logo, title/subtitle, gold glow and "Apple product reveal" polish produced a finished ten-second motion graphic. Revisions (bigger bolder title, more glow, 20% slower pace) are one more prompt, not reopening a project file.

**Built-in library:** Lower thirds (Clean Bar, Bold Block, Dark Card, Mask Reveal, News Ticker), captions (Pill Karaoke, Kinetic Slam, Neon Glow, Glitch RGB, Particle Burst), transitions (Cinematic Zoom, Light Leak, Whip Pan, Cross Warp Morph), social overlays (YouTube Subscribe, Instagram/TikTok Follow, X Post, Spotify Now-Playing), motion graphics (stat cards, flowcharts, checklists, animated maps, logo outros), VFX (Liquid Glass, Shatter, Portal, Magnetic, 3D iPhone/MacBook mockups).

**Worked example:** an 8-prompt SME promo video (business coach, 8-week programme) — master brief → scene-by-scene plan → opening/problem/talking-head/social-proof/outro scenes → audio pass → three export versions (landscape, vertical, square) correctly reframed, not just resized. Total time: ~25–30 minutes, versus a freelance editor's typical £400–£1,200 and 5–7 day turnaround for comparable output.

**Takeaway:** tools that used to require a specialist and a production budget now run on a laptop and a clear prompt — the same automation shift CodeSquad builds toward, applied to video.

### SEO Is No Longer Enough: A Beginner's Guide to AEO and GEO in the Age of AI Search
*AEO / SEO · August 10, 2026 (v2) and July 27, 2026 (original) · /blog/seo-aeo-geo-ai-search-guide-2 and /blog/seo-aeo-geo-ai-search-guide*

**Traditional SEO** (Search Engine Optimization) has four areas: Technical SEO (fast loading, mobile-friendly, crawlable, HTTPS, clean architecture, canonical URLs, sitemaps, structured data), On-page SEO (titles, headings, keywords, URLs, internal links, alt text, meta descriptions), Off-page SEO (backlinks, brand mentions, reviews, directories, partnerships, media coverage), Content SEO (service pages, comparison guides, tutorials, case studies, FAQs, original research).

**AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)** structures content so search engines and AI assistants can identify a clear, direct answer to a question — e.g. leading with "Lead follow-up automation is a system that automatically responds to, qualifies, nurtures, and routes new enquiries using tools such as email, SMS, CRM updates, and internal notifications," then expanding. Answer engines include Google featured snippets/AI Overviews, voice assistants, ChatGPT search, Bing Copilot. Google explicitly says content doesn't need to be chopped into unnatural tiny chunks — it should still be written primarily for people.

**GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)** increases the likelihood a brand/site/product is discovered, trusted, cited or recommended in AI-generated answers, which often synthesize one combined response from multiple sources rather than ten links. GEO rewards genuine first-hand expertise, original examples, accurate/consistent company information, author credentials, independent reviews, and case studies with specific methodology — generic summarized content is easy to reproduce and easy to replace.

**SEO vs AEO vs GEO:** SEO gets the page discovered and ranked; AEO makes the content the best direct answer; GEO makes the brand/content a trusted source in generative answers. Google treats generative-AI optimization as part of SEO, not a separate discipline, and warns against "AEO/GEO hacks" like unnecessary AI-specific files or buying artificial mentions.

**10-step optimization checklist:** (1) start with real customer questions from sales/support/ops; (2) answer the main question early, before a long intro; (3) publish first-hand expertise from real project work; (4) create detailed, honestly-numbered case studies; (5) strengthen your brand entity (consistent NAP, leadership, social profiles, Google Business Profile); (6) use structured data correctly (Organization, LocalBusiness, Article, Product, Service, Review, FAQ schema) — not a shortcut, but accurate markup; (7) make the site crawlable (robots.txt, noindex, canonicals, JS rendering, sitemap accuracy); (8) build authority beyond the website (reviews, partnerships, podcasts, directories, earned media); (9) keep important content current; (10) measure business results (impressions, CTR, qualified enquiries, assisted conversions, branded search, AI citations), including Search Console's generative-AI reporting where available.

**Common mistakes:** treating SEO as obsolete, publishing large volumes of generic AI content, optimizing only for machines at the expense of readability, expecting guaranteed AI citations (no platform can promise a specific citation every time).

**FAQ:** Is SEO being replaced by AI search? No — Google's generative features run on its core ranking/quality systems; AEO/GEO extend SEO, they don't replace it. Can a business "rank" in ChatGPT? Not via fixed numbered positions — improve chances through accessible, authoritative, relevant content and accurate brand information; inclusion isn't guaranteed. Do I need an llms.txt file for GEO? Google states llms.txt neither improves nor harms visibility in Google Search or its generative features; other platforms may treat it differently, so base implementation on documented platform requirements rather than marketing claims. Is AEO only FAQ pages? No — it applies to service pages, guides, product pages, comparisons and support docs generally. How long does AEO/GEO take? No universal timeline; depends on technical health, authority, competition, content quality and how fast platforms re-crawl.

### How Businesses Are Losing Money Without Realizing It: The Hidden Cost of Slow Lead Response
*AI Automation · August 7, 2026 · /blog/how-businesses-lose-money-slow-lead-response*

A business can spend heavily on Google Ads, generate plenty of leads, and still lose money if it responds too slowly — a prospect (e.g. someone searching for a med spa) often contacts several businesses at once, and whichever responds first has the advantage. Ideally, communication should begin almost immediately: a confirmation message by SMS/email the moment a form is submitted, then a scheduled follow-up (call or SMS) the next day if there's no reply — leads shouldn't disappear just because nobody followed up fast enough.

**The bigger problem is fragmented visibility:** as a business grows, Google Ads, SMS, calls, email marketing, content and SEO often live in separate systems, so a founder asking "how are our ads performing?" gets conflicting answers (ad quality vs. lead quality vs. sales follow-up) with no way to verify which explanation is right.

**The fix: a centralized business dashboard** tracking ad spend/performance, lead generation, lead response times, SMS activity, calls, email marketing, offers, customer responses, content performance and SEO activity in one place — so decisions are based on actual performance data rather than individual opinions, and underperforming spend can be identified and reallocated.

**You don't need to automate everything** — identify what's actually costing money, where opportunities are lost, what you currently can't see, and which processes should be faster, then build systems around those specific points rather than chasing every new tool.

**Two things to focus on:** (1) respond to leads quickly — timing determines whether a prospect stays or moves to a competitor; (2) create visibility across the business — you can't manage what you can't see across ads, calls, SMS, email, content and SEO.

**Bottom line:** businesses often lose money not from too few leads but from slow response to the leads they already paid for, and from spending on activities they can't properly evaluate because data is scattered. Fix: respond faster, measure what matters, centralize visibility, identify what works, reduce what doesn't.

### From "Microneedling Near Me" to Booked: The SEO Strategy for Med Spas
*AI Automation · September 21, 2026 · /blog/microneedling-seo-med-spas*

Patients search for microneedling at different decision stages — location-based searches, treatment comparisons, pricing queries — so a med spa's job is to appear in those searches and give visitors a compelling reason to book.

**Build a dedicated microneedling service page** rather than folding it into a generic services list: explain the treatment, the concerns it addresses, the patient experience, recovery guidance, FAQs and scheduling. Write for patient understanding first, search engines second. Create separate pages for distinct variations (e.g. RF microneedling) since they target different search intent.

**Don't ignore local SEO** — med spas win on local visibility, not national rankings. Optimize the Google Business Profile, website location data, reviews and service info for the specific practice location; local results and map packs often outrank organic listings for location-based queries.

**Create content around real patient questions** — effectiveness for scars, session frequency, sensation during the procedure, post-treatment expectations, technique differences, cost — written to genuinely help, with natural paths into the relevant treatment page rather than keyword stuffing.

**SEO is no longer just about Google** — patients increasingly use AI tools to research and compare, so sites need to be clearly understandable to both search engines and AI systems regarding business identity, treatments, location and expertise. This combines SEO, AEO and GEO, with an emphasis on trustworthy content over keyword manipulation.

**Google Ads complement SEO** — SEO builds organically over time; ads capture high-intent searches immediately. The funnel: Search → Ad → Landing Page → Lead → Follow-Up → Booking. Landing pages need clear messaging, trust indicators and a consultation-booking mechanism.

**Getting the lead isn't enough** — delayed response cools interest even after a successful ad click. This is why lead generation needs to be paired with automated notifications, CRM, email/SMS sequences, appointment workflows and tracking so the team can respond fast.

**CodeSquad's approach:** integrate SEO, Google Ads, local search, AI-focused strategy, automation and conversion systems into one framework — examining the full patient pathway (SEO supporting Maps visibility, content supporting services, ads directing to the right pages, leads enabling follow-up, analytics tracking opportunity) rather than treating each marketing channel in isolation.
